Astronomers just found three stars born together that took three different paths.
A Chinese telescope called FAST spotted a pulsar in 2020: a dead star spinning once every 3.2 milliseconds.
It has a white dwarf partner. They circle each other every eight days.
But the pulsar seemed to be slowing about a hundred times too fast. Something was pulling on it.
The answer was a third star, about the mass of the Sun, circling the pair every 73 and a half years.
Its gravity shifts the pulse timing, like a hidden hand tugging a clock.
The biggest star, about 20 Suns, exploded. The middle one became a white dwarf. The outer one is still alive.
That makes it only the second pulsar triple known, and the first with a living star.
